Salantai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klaipėdos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Salantai was known for the 'Musar' rabbis and intellectuals who traced their roots to the town — part of the broader Musar ethical movement documented elsewhere in this collection. Seven headstones of Salantai Jews who died in the late 19th century can still be found at the old Jewish cemetery in Jerusalem. The entire Jewish community was murdered in summer 1941 at three sites, including one near this cemetery; burials continued here even during the community's confinement in a temporary ghetto shortly before its destruction. A 1991 memorial plaque at the entrance was placed at the initiative of Jakovas Bunka of Plungė, documented elsewhere in this collection, and the Salantai community; nearby stands a wooden totem pole depicting an old man reaching toward the sky above a kneeling woman, inscribed: 'For the 405 Jews of Salantai murdered in July 1941.'
